Class ObjectPool<T>

A thread-safe object pool for reusing instances of type T.

public sealed class ObjectPool<T> where T : class

T

The reference type being pooled.

Remarks

Uses a thread-safe ConcurrentBag<T> to store available instances. Provide a Func<TResult> to create new instances and an optional Action<T> to reset instances when they are returned to the pool. If extension is needed, prefer a wrapper that delegates to ObjectPool rather than deriving from it.

Methods

Clear()

Removes all objects currently stored in the pool's internal container.

public void Clear()

Remarks

This clears only the available instances held by the pool; instances already checked out via Rent() are not affected. The underlying operation uses the thread-safe ConcurrentBag<T> implementation.

GetDisposableHandle()

Creates a disposable handle that wraps a pooled instance. The handle will return the instance to this pool when the handle is disposed.

public PooledObjectHandle<T> GetDisposableHandle()

Returns

PooledObjectHandle<T>

A PooledObjectHandle<T> containing a pooled T instance.

Remarks

Use the returned handle in a using statement (or dispose it manually) to ensure the instance is returned to the pool promptly. This method obtains a single instance via Rent().

Rent()

Retrieves an instance from the pool if one is available; otherwise creates a new instance using the factory provided to the pool constructor.

public T Rent()

Returns

T

A pooled instance of T. The caller should return the instance to the pool by calling Return(T) when finished.

Return(T)

Returns an instance to the pool. The instance will be reset using the optional reset delegate (if provided) and then added back to the internal storage for reuse.

public void Return(T instance)

Parameters

instance T

The instance to return to the pool. Must not be null.
